query: We need signed session tokens. Should we write our own signing algorithm to avoid a dependency, or use the language standard library? Recommend an approach and say what evidence could change it.
expected_behavior: States the required token behavior and checks the language/runtime and existing dependencies before proposing new code
Recommends a vetted existing cryptographic implementation when it meets the token format and security requirements
Preserves signature verification, key handling, expiry and authorization checks at the relevant trust boundary
Names concrete compatibility or security evidence that could change the implementation choice
Does not treat minimum dependency count or an analogy as proof that custom cryptography is simpler or safe
